tasks.title: Clear the burnt debris
dialogue: Grandpa's café... there's nothing left but ash.
Nell Marlowe? Didn't think you'd ever come back.
Neither did I. But the Lantern Café deserves better than this.

tasks.title: Lay a new floor
dialogue: The fire started in the back. Odd, the stove was never used at night.
I think I've said too much.

tasks.title: Build a coffee counter
dialogue: Nell! I brought croissants. Old habit.
Ada! You still bake for the whole island?
Someone has to. Now, about that counter...

tasks.title: Set out two tables
dialogue: That's Pip. Your grandpa fed him every morning. He's yours now.

tasks.title: Hang the old lantern
dialogue: The lantern survived. Grandpa said it lit the way home for sailors.
Charming. Though the harbour is due for... redevelopment.
We'll talk. Welcome home, Miss Marlowe.

tasks.title: Open the doors
dialogue: First coffee in three years. Tastes like the old days.
The Lantern Café is open again!

tasks.title: Fix the water pipes
dialogue: No water. The pipes are fine, so where did it go?
The island springs dried up the night of the fire. That's no coincidence.
Juno. I study the island's plants. And its secrets.

tasks.title: Clear the terrace
dialogue: The terrace used to be packed on summer nights.
Your grandpa and the mayor argued out here the week before the fire.

tasks.title: Plant herb boxes
dialogue: Herbs only grow where water returns. Look: sprouts already.
The puzzle springs... someone restored them.

tasks.title: Put up an awning
dialogue: An awning? You're settling in, I see.
Then you'll want to read this letter. Your grandfather's debts didn't burn with the café.

tasks.title: Find grandpa's ledger
dialogue: He kept a ledger hidden under the counter. Always did.
Every debt is paid... in full. The mayor lied.
Then ask yourself why he wants this harbour so badly.

tasks.title: Restore the fountain
dialogue: The spring under the café is the island's oldest. Whoever owns the café owns the water.

tasks.title: Rebuild the kitchen
dialogue: A real kitchen! Now I can teach you my berry pie.
Ada, the night of the fire, you were here late. Why?
...I was meeting someone. I can't say who. Not yet.

tasks.title: Repair the dock
dialogue: Boats can moor here again. Customers by sea!
I saw a lantern on the water that night. Moving toward the café.
Couldn't tell. But it had the town hall's flag.

tasks.title: String festival lights
dialogue: The whole harbour is glowing. The island feels alive.
Impressive. The council will want to... inspect.
Let them. I've got nothing to hide. Have you?

tasks.title: Read the burnt letter
dialogue: Half a letter, from Grandpa to Ada: 'If anything happens, protect the spring.'
He knew someone wanted it. I promised him. I just didn't know who.
We're going to find out. Together.

tasks.title: Build a music stage
dialogue: A harbour festival. Everyone will come.
Even the person who lit the fire.

tasks.title: Host the Lantern Festival
dialogue: ...Fine. I took the boat that night. I wanted the deed, not a fire.
When I got there, the café was already burning. Someone else was there.
To be continued, lass. Some secrets take more than one night.

tasks.title: Turn the back room into a meeting hall
dialogue: The council wants to meet here now. The café of all places.
Where else? Everyone ends up here sooner or later.

tasks.title: Pin the clues to a board
dialogue: Deed, lighter, logbook, lens... and Rafe's story.
He says the café was already burning when he arrived.

tasks.title: Rebuild Ada's big oven
dialogue: I smelled lamp oil that night. Not cigar smoke. Oil.
Oil... like the ropes the Rope Isles traders soak?

tasks.title: Plant the memory garden
dialogue: One tree for every island that came back.
Four so far. Your grandfather would want six.

tasks.title: Paint the archipelago map
dialogue: Verdant, Ember Reef, Lantern Bay, Stone Steps... and the Rope Isles.
Rafe's skiff was seen there. And a trader who sells lamp oil.

tasks.title: Launch the Rope Isles ferry
dialogue: The ferry's ready. The isles are a maze of ropes and tides.
Then I'll learn to cross them. Someone else lit that fire.

tasks.title: Clear out the old cellar
dialogue: Twenty barrels of lamp oil, bought by Silas. I knew that smell.
Silas sold moonflower lamps. He knew every garden on the islands.

tasks.title: Hang moonflower lamps
dialogue: These lamps glow without oil. Moon Grove flowers, dried and sealed.
Then why would Silas need twenty barrels of oil?

tasks.title: Read Grandpa's last letter
dialogue: 'Silas wants the spring for his grove. If I say no, he says the café will pay.'

tasks.title: Seat the six-island council
dialogue: I'll stand in front of all six islands and say what I saw.
Even the mayor's grown a spine. Pass the bread.

tasks.title: Fit the night boat
dialogue: Moon Grove only opens at night. The flowers close by day.

tasks.title: Sail for Moon Grove
dialogue: Bring a lantern. The grove is dark where the moss has spread.

tasks.title: Welcome Nell home
dialogue: She's back! And the grove is glowing again.
Silas confessed to the council. He's rebuilding what he burned, stone by stone.

tasks.title: Frame the harbour deed
dialogue: The spring belongs to everyone. Your grandfather made sure of it.

tasks.title: Write the six-island menu
dialogue: Reef skewers, lighthouse candles, terrace tea, rope-market fruit and moon cakes.
A café that tastes like the whole archipelago.

tasks.title: Raise the festival stage
dialogue: I'll carry the planks. It's the least I can do.

tasks.title: Light a lantern for every island
dialogue: Verdant, Ember Reef, Lantern Bay, Stone Steps, Rope Isles, Moon Grove.
Six lights. Just like the old days.

tasks.title: Hold the Festival of Six Isles
dialogue: Grandpa, the café is open. The water runs. The islands are one again.
And tomorrow we'll need twice as many cakes.

intro: Thirty springs flowing again... and the old harbour is still in ruins.
The Lantern Café. Your grandfather's pride, before the fire.
Then I'll bring it back. Coffee, bread, fresh catch. One order at a time.
Drag two of the same thing together and you'll make something better. Folks here are hungry, lass.
